routes.description: Establish that Paul understood Jesus as an earthly historical person by combining Pauline biographical and familial references with an earthly reading of the crucifying rulers and corroboration from sources connected to Paul and the Gospel tradition.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the Pauline references are best explained as ordinary historical claims, the rulers passage situates the crucifixion among human authorities, and the proposed Acts and Gospel corroboration remains sufficiently independent and reliable to reinforce that reading.

motionBridge.description: Show that the cumulative evidence is better explained by Paul referring to a human Jesus who lived and was crucified on Earth than by a wholly celestial setting for the saving events.

centralBridges.description: Establish that Pauline references to ancestry, birth, teachings, associates, betrayal, and execution supply meaningful historical particularity.
Establish from the context of First Corinthians that the rulers responsible for the crucifixion are human authorities, even if spiritual forces also participated.
Show that references to James and other brothers of the Lord are most coherently understood as biological relationships to Jesus.
Establish that Acts is substantially reliable and connected to a companion of Paul, making its historical Jesus relevant to reconstructing Paul's understanding.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Defend a sufficiently broad Pauline corpus so that relevant historical references are not excluded solely by disputed authorship judgments.
Show that dispersed incidental correspondences among Gospel narratives are more expected on historical information than deliberate literary harmonization.

routes.description: Establish that Paul's accepted letters do not securely locate Jesus's ministry, death, and resurrection on Earth, while their cosmic language permits a flesh-bearing celestial figure killed by demonic rulers in a mythic heavenly realm.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if Pauline biographical and familial expressions remain materially ambiguous, the rulers and cosmology make a heavenly crucifixion viable, and Acts and Gospel narratives cannot independently import a later earthly biography into Paul's letters.

motionBridge.description: Show that the earliest relevant Pauline evidence remains compatible with, and materially supports, a mortal embodied Jesus whose death and resurrection occurred in a celestial rather than terrestrial realm.

centralBridges.description: Establish that the accepted Pauline letters lack an unambiguous earthly ministry or terrestrial location for Jesus's death and resurrection.
Show that the rulers of the age can be celestial demonic powers and that their concealed knowledge and interests fit that interpretation.
Establish that ancient cosmology allowed heavenly counterparts of earthly places, objects, and practices, making a celestial crucifixion intelligible.
Show that Acts and the Gospels are too disputed, literary, dependent, or historically unstable to determine what Paul believed about Jesus.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Show that Pauline brother-of-the-Lord language can identify an ordinary baptized Christian rather than a biological sibling of Jesus.
Supply the comparative possibility that a savior cult could later place a nonhistorical divine figure into an earthly narrative.

sections.title: Pauline Biography, Silence, and Corpus Scope
sections.rationale: The motion turns first on whether the relevant Pauline letters contain historical markers sufficient to locate Jesus on Earth, and whether the admissible Pauline corpus expands or restricts that evidence.

sections.title: The Rulers and the Realm of Crucifixion
sections.rationale: The identity of the rulers of the age and the cosmological intelligibility of heavenly counterparts directly distinguish an earthly execution by human authorities from a celestial passion involving demonic powers.

sections.title: James and the Brothers of the Lord
sections.rationale: Whether Paul's references identify biological relatives or members of a baptized cultic family is among the most direct disputes over historical particularity within the Pauline evidence.

sections.title: Acts, Pauline Chronology, and Companion Authorship
sections.rationale: Acts can connect Paul to a thoroughly historical Jesus only if its chronology, factual reliability, first-person narration, and claimed relationship to a Pauline companion survive the competing literary explanation.

sections.title: Gospel Independence and Undesigned Coincidences
sections.rationale: The evidential value of cross-Gospel correspondences depends on whether dispersed details reflect independent historical information or deliberate adaptation and harmonization of earlier narrative sources.
